title: An early 19.46-day GJ 163 wave gives an uncertain later prediction gain
abstract: We test whether a disputed 19.46-day wave in GJ 163 predicts later HARPS velocities. A wave fitted to 155 early exposures lowers weighted error by 5.07 percent in 48 later exposures, after separate fits of known-period nuisance terms. A 30-day block resampling range is -16.13 to +23.29 percent and includes early fit uncertainty. Thus, this test gives no clear confirmation of a stable wave. Extraction, nuisance, nearby-period, positive-signal and recovery controls measure the scope of the test. All reductions use HARPS spectra. No independent instrument confirmation, new planet or unique physical cause is established. The external database is excluded. Code, aggregate evidence, an original figure, exact input provenance and retrieval instructions are included.
